Another disappointment is all the weapons break after 2-3 hits. It seemed like the best weapon was grabbing an opponent and using their body as a weapon swinging them around and hitting the other opponents but after about 5 minutes of doing this it seems that it doesn’t actually do any damage at all. Even grabbing a guy by his head and slamming it into a table or counter top repeatedly seems to do no damage. On the balcony level you can throw opponents off the balcony but they come right back up the elevator like instantaneously. You throw them off and in less than a second they’re walking back in the door. I played the game about 15-20 minutes and that was it. I had already seen and done everything and completely lost interest. Just another cheap gimmick game for psvr. It sucks that we get tons of cheap games that don’t have any real replay value and can be beaten in an hour or less. I would compare about 95% of vr games to cell phone games because of the time it takes to beat them. In most cases cell phone games actually have more replay value than the psvr games. Game_Name: DISSIDIA FINAL FANTASY NT Free Edition
Author: @One_Man_Army919
Comment: Although I agree dissidia NT is a step down from its predecessors, this guy doesn’t know what he’s talking about. Bravery attacks boost the power of your HP attacks. You don’t lose all of your bravery if you miss an HP attack. Second this guy literally changed the HUD from its smaller default setting to the bigger arcade version then complained about it? Then he complained about the game not having enough characters? The previous game had 31 characters and NT has 28 in the base game along with 6 additional characters. The summon battles are fun and the only time you lose a health bar is when YOU die by an attack not when your allies do. In the end dissidia NT falls short of its predecessors. The decision to remove the rpg elements and a solid 1v1 gameplay is what really hurt this title. The lack of story and character interactions within the game makes it feel empty sometimes but there’s still fun to be had within the game. The 3v3 is a bold and new take on the battle system having teamwork at the core of the gameplay. When players work as a TEAM they can pull off satisfying combos, summon deities to turn the tide of a battle or crush the opposing team. Summons also grants players with buffs and abilities before and after they are summoned. The 3v3 gameplay adds a layer of strategic value to the combat system. Players can use a variety of buffs, debuffs, and other unique abilities to aid them in battle. Choosing the right abilities to compliment your characters play style is essential to victory. Every character has their own play style and unique abilities/skill keeping the gameplay interesting. Dissidia NT may not be what fans expected but it’s not an entirely bad game. A 7/10 is fair in my opinion.

Author: @FrancoDMatz
Comment:
You clearly underestimated this game immensely. All the 'issues' you've spoken about are not even issues at all. I'd say you should play the game some more and get used to it, then you'll find how enjoyable it is.

In terms of attacks, etc, you just have to get used to the mechanics of them and you'll find that the game was engineered very well. You just have to get the timing right in terms of when you avoid enemy attacks and when you dish out your own so you can land hits. You totally didn't understand about targeting as well. The game has an auto-target feature so that is why you'll find yourself hitting a player closest to you; but you can actually pick out opponents to target by tapping on the character or tapping on the character's icon on the top right. This will put a target on the opponent, and tapping again will remove the target.

Dodging is all about timing as well. Keep a look out for opponent attacks so you can dodge them. If you get your timing right, you can get a perfect dodge which will make you temporarily invincible thus allowing for an opportunity to counterattack.

Furthermore, characters are added to the game regularly...I would say every month sees an average of at least 2 new characters added to the game. With the multitude of characters in the ONE PIECE series itself, you can expect that there will always be new characters to be added in the game.

Progression is fair because you really have to put effort into building your characters. There's various ways to do so even if you're not a whale. You can't just expect to start playing a game and then after a few days have all maxed out characters. Be realistic please. Building up your character roster should be part of enjoying the game.

I like that I get to play a game using all the characters I love (or hate) in the ONE PIECE series. There's different exciting stages and soundtracks. The skills are amazing, and you get to adjust how much attack power you can dish out or defensive abilities you can tank by upgrading and equipping appropriate medals to your characters. There's different game modes which rotate every month aside from the main league mode.

My issues with the game are (and these are issues I think other experienced players will relate to):

• Cheating players that use third party software or hacks.

• The game's poor matchmaking feature - sometimes you get matched with shitty teammates or bots whilst the opponents are all real players who have incredible ranks.

• Japan version vs Global version. Japan version is always favoured by the developers and will get new stuff first or better offers.

• Poor support from the developers, Bandai Namco. You send inquiries and support tickets and they just talk shit and never resolve anything. I've been complaining to them about bots and matchmaking for ages and they just say it's 'working as intended'. It is false advertising considering how they say "You will be matched with players of similar abilities and ranks."


Thanks for that review though. Hopefully it might get the developers to wake up and address real issues with the game.

Author: @Sebbie_C
Comment: Selling the game for profit would get Besto Games (the developers) in hot water with Cover Inc., the company that owns Hololive as their Vtuber brand. However, Cover has a derivative works license that allows for the creation of fan games such as Idol Showdown and HoloCure (a Vampire Survivors-like game with a Hololive theme). Such fan projects are allowed under this license so long as the creators do not try to sell them for profit in any way (though donations are allowed). Cover has always been pretty awesome in this regard and there are many Hololive-themed fan games and projects out there. Idol Showdown marks the release of a fan-made game that was in development for two years and crafted by a small team of fan developers. They have already been hard at work patching and fixing issues with the game (they even live-patched the game so that Calliope Mori and Tsunomaki Watame- two Hololive talents from the EN and JP branches, respectively) could play multiplayer matches with each other; they even were watching Koefficient's stream and patched out an exploit with Botan's moves that he was using in real-time. This really is an awesome little game from a team of devoted developers who obviously put time and love and effort into what they've made, and it shows.

Author: @Scyushi
Comment:
While I LOVE what this game could have been, I'm severely disappointed in what it isn't.. the art is top tier and the gameplay is pretty solid albeit very buggy at the moment, but my problem with The Unliving is the general lack of progression.
See, when I play a roguelike, it either has to be 
A: SO fun to do a run that I don't care if I start from scratch every single time (like Risk of Rain 2, Rogue Legacy or Dead Cells) 
or B: Slowly gives me more and more permanent upgrades that make each run easier and easier (Samurai Bringer is a fantastic roguelike to feel OP)
Maybe I'm the odd one out with my opinion on this, but one of the reasons I enjoy playing a necromancer is the idea of having my army do all the dirty work, but The Unliving manages to make it feel like I'm the one doing all the work with my units more-so acting like a blockade for enemies, rather than an opposing force.

Anyways that's my thoughts on it. I had a lot of fun making this review, and the first 2 hours of The Unliving were amazing. I went into this game with high hopes and kept playing it, assuring myself "it'll get better, just wait" but was left disappointed.

Thanks for listing to my rant and watching my video <3

As of December 30th, 2021, the Quaver difficulty system is still sometimes inconsistent. Author: @zenithdragon
Comment:
Just gonna list my thoughts as the video plays.

I think that a lot of my opinions on the monetization have changed since the first week of release. 2 ways to look at it is through cosmetics and through gameplay. For cosmetics, I don't think it is that bad but I have always disliked gacha leaders. I think the gacha leaders are set up terribly since there are 4 and you need 3 of each to get everything. Granted I don't care about getting the visages for Shadowverse Park but you used to get the alt art and the leader from one pull which is annoying. The high cost of the old leaders is egregious for those that really want them. The split up of seers globes and other premium cosmetics into multiple items is frustrating and the vial cost is too high but whatever most people aren't out here making a full premium deck. So, I think the cosmetic monetization is mostly there to exploit whales. 

The gameplay part of monetization is pretty annoying although I think it is mostly because of how f2p friendly Shadowverse classic was. The reward system is a bit less than it was in Shadowverse classic but the visible issue is the increase in pack cost from 100 to 500 rupies without a shift in rupie rewards to match. You used to get enough for at least a pack a day through mission rewards and now it is considerably less. Shadowverse Park has some various rewards that almost offset it but it is diluted with cosmetic rewards. It is offset by the free daily pack but that pack doesn't count toward pack points for the gacha leaders/animated art styles and doesn't count toward the 10 pack pity timer for legendaries. The pity timer is a great addition. The battle pass is less rewarding than it was in classic but the cost is reduced and the time for it has been reduced so it is probably fine but we won't really know until we get to the intended 2 month per set cadence. Speaking of, really going to be tough to keep up since they are dropping the next set one month after launch and set 3 comes out a month and a half after that. Depending on the set sizes that could be very detrimental to a f2p or new player experience. Even with these issues, the game isn't bad f2p and would probably be on par with most f2p ccgs if it wasn't for the fact you can't vial cards unless you have at least 3 copies. That alone makes it much harder to get an initial deck going and based on your pulls you may not even be able to play a class you want for a while. It doesn't help that a lot of classes need a bunch of legendaries to be good.

The sequel, from my understanding, was mostly due to an attempt at balancing the classes better and updating a very old client. The client is like 10 years old at this point and I think they were having trouble implementing certain mechanics and dealing with file sizes. The onboarding was also extremely dated and everyone assumed they were going to do better the second time around which it is better but not by much. I also secretly suspect it is because they wanted to use their own game engine and the original was made in unity. Remember back when unity wanted to charge devs in perpetuity based on game downloads?

Shadowverse Park I have turned around on. It is pretty fun to mess around in and I think the weekend tournaments they have planned can really help with a sense of community surrounding the game that isn't possible in other ccgs. I just wish you could access everything from both the home screen as well as Shadowverse Park. Not being able to see the park missions on the home screen and not being able to see missions in the park easily is annoying. Some of the weekly park missions are dumb like messaging a friend and is just busywork. Also the filter has been updated and you can now say "is".

The lack of single-player content in inexcusable. The game was delayed a year and we get one short story with barely any rewards. I understand the want to drip feed content to keep people coming back but how am I going to have any investment in the overall story when there is barely a start to it in the current game. 

With regards to gameplay, aggro and control sorta exist? Only real aggro deck imo is storm dragon which is decent enough but it is only because you get your damage out before your opponent has a chance to remove your guys. Sword kinda has an aggro mode for the midrange deck but it is a tad highrolly and gets dunked on by apollo in the early game. I think they didn't want aggro to be too strong with the extra play point going second and that is why all the early game cards have trash statlines. You could also play aggro abyss but that is cope imo. Control is currently locked out because haven is the only real control option currently and they have no real wincon in the late game. Also Cocytus being in one of the most popular decks, spellboost rune, (as well as in some control haven and abyss lists) really locks out haven from just running the opponent out of resources. It is unfortunate because haven is probably my favorite class currently since I just really enjoy the back and forth gameplay it provides and the value from amulets. Darkhaven Grace is my favorite card because of just how valuable it is throughout the game. Class distinction is actually very well done in this first set. Each class feels very unique. On your bit on portalcraft, turns out the gameplay for artifacts kinda ignores the big mech unless they really need it. They just focus on cheating out the 5 cost guys for burn or removal with cards like Alouette, Doomwright Ward and then abuse Orchis as a finisher. Abyss has also made a turnaround in the meta and is the actual most expensive class where the optimal deck is running three of each abyss legendary and 2 or 3 copies of Olivia and sometimes 1 Cocytus. The deck apparently matches relatively well into portal and sword but is tough to pilot since most of your cards are just not that good and you are hard carried by Argavy for board clear, Medusa for board clear as well as maybe a cheeky lethal if it survives a turn, and Cerberus as your only real wincon that can technically highroll you into 15 damage with setup. Haven is looking like the least popular. I think that the issue you bring up with lack of deck options for each class is solely due to the small card pool like you mentioned.


On the paid vs unpaid crystals, from my understanding that is due to laws in certain countries forcing them to make a distinction. I don't believe they have any difference in game currently. Also, the only way to get the crystals is through paying or getting them through the paid battle pass. The cost per pack is slightly tough to gauge against other games because of how the deck structure is different, the pack size is different, and different pity systems on high rarity cards. Also, the best deal currently is through the cygames store which is a better "value" for crystals if one intends to pay. Optimally, one would buy that pack and maybe the small one-time packs and then only use those crystals on the battlepass and the once a day 50 crystal pack. A lot of the math I have seen btw on the subreddit has been kinda off but is probably good enough for generalities. Speaking of, the subreddit in my experience has been real bad with people bitching and moaning constantly about either the rewards being too little or because tier 1 decks exist In my experience, about 200 packs got me to the point where I can play most meta decks. I think I am missing like 8 golds and maybe 15 legendaries from having a complete collection. The problem is going to be if every set is going to be as large as this first one. Hopefully they are smaller since they plan to release them so often but we'll see. The daily mission timer is annoying but in theory is better than if it was based on a server reset since the cooldown is 21 hours and not 24. In theory, if you play extremely optimally you get an extra set of missions every like week and a half. In practice, I found it makes no difference and is just slightly annoying if your schedule doesn't line up with when the missions reset. I honestly don't think the monetization is that bad but maybe I am growing too accustomed to the microtransaction filled hell we currently live in.

I think the reason the game is getting so much flak in reviews is because of all the people that played Shadowverse classic seeing a clearly worse f2p experience, the obviously bad cosmetic monetization, the confusing menus (although that may just be a skill issue on my end), the mediocre if not bad tutorial, and the difficulty in making your first good deck when f2p (cheapest options are probably Roach forest, dragon, and sword but roach is not new player friendly). The frequency of events currently has been the only thing nice about the f2p experience right now, even though the rewards are less than in Shadowverse classic. Like the treasure trove of rupies event had significantly worse rewards and the currently running chest event has worse rewards than in classic. Whenever I think about how to make the f2p experience better I think about how they probably only need to make 1 change to satisfy most people and 2 changes if they want it to be good. 1. Allow people to vial any card they want (that would solve most problems) and 2. double most rupie payouts to help offset how much it costs to buy a pack. I think if they did that it would make the game significantly better for new players and keep f2p players around to keep the playerbase up. I also guess a small balance patch could also help with some of the outliers when it comes to overperforming cards like Orchis, Alouette, Anne & Grea, and there is probably some card in Roach forest that needs hit but who cares when there will be a meta shakeup in 2 weeks anyway.

Great video as always and the ending reminds me that I still need to get around to finishing Xenoblade Chronicles.

Author: @Gutnarm
Comment:
I've clocked a couple thousand hours in LIF:YO over the years, the "early access small map low pop private server" variant of the game; our community server was "enforced RP-PVP, fair play, no offlining, no trolling, no cheesing", with a couple active admins 👌. OMG, did the clans terraform and build a LOT of nice villages, towns, even cities with keeps and castle walls, fairgrounds fit for duels and jousting, leveled cobbled "horse highways" between towns, waystops at major crossings, you get the picture.
...then the MMO part hit, and our small server's community basically went up in a puff of smoke within a few weeks as half the people stayed behind/stopped playing, while the other half got lost trying to find each other after randomly spawning gear- and skill-less all over the massive MMO map's border regions (while being chewed up by the environment, wild animals, and your ubiquitous Russian PVP clans who - naturally, like on the official servers - already had their goons semi-geared up and roaming). So: death > respawn > start from scratch in yet another random border location. LIF:MMO ain't like ...aah, RUST, for example: it'll take you hours, *real hours*, to get from A to B.
*edit* I did like 40, 50 hours in LIF:MMO, really trying to hook up with whoever of our community was still around, trying to get a common staging area, a rallying point, RESPAWN POINT, set up somewhere. it didn't work out, and eventually I called it quits.

Author: @saltheart2023
Comment: As stated... this game is not for everyone...  it is certainly a grind to do most anything. I have been playing for many many years now....  will take a break for months here and there and always seem to come back...   No other game seems to compare (for me at least) ----  Simply put...  It can be AMAZING!   If you take the time to learn the "basics" of how the interface works... how to gather resources, refine those resources into more usable materials, then use those materials to craft your own tools, structures, fences, furniture, forges, ovens, etc. it can be So Very Rewarding! The whole system is intricate and there are few (if any) games with a crafting system as involved (reminds me a little of the old Star Wars Galaxies crafting from long ago) -- gather resources, refine resources into usable materials, craft said materials into the parts you need, then use those parts to craft whatever it is you are making --- a house, a forge, an oven, a fence, a tool, some armor, a weapon, etc.  --   You Stake a Claim and create a Deed that becomes your area... Your Homestead to do with as you please.   Terraform the landscape to how you like it - mine tunnels to find minerals such as Iron - plant crops, raise (and breed) animals, fish in a local lake or river for meat for cooking, plant trees for later harvesting, build a house, villa or castle, cook food to improve your nutrition which helps you with your skill gains.  Possibilities are endless  ----  you can do Free to Play up to 20 skill in any of the 115 (???) different skills - to go above 20 you must buy Premium for around 8.00 Euros (don't quote me on that)  per month?  --- and you can purchase the In-Game Currency on the website as well to pay for the Upkeep on your Deed.  Anyway, if you are looking for a Medieval Survival / Homesteading type of game with a VERY friendly and dedicated community and deep crafting / gathering systems... then WURM Online may be worth looking into... It's Free to Try and there are many youtube vids to help out with the basics of the Interface.   Cheers!  Hope to see you in-game!  :-)   I'm on the Cadence Server (Northern Islands)

But they are books with a cool/intriguing premise, fun story-line, a quick pace and a mystery the main protagonist has to solve. Simple book. But fantastically well done for what it is. That is why people give it 5/5. (Or 4.5 out 5 in the case of Petrik Leo).

Author: @IGN
Comment: UPDATE: It turns out that the framerate can in fact go above 30fps on the Xbox One X and PS4 Pro. There is an option to unlock the framerate in the menu. As stated, we reviewed this on PC, but we'd been explicitly told by Deep Silver prior to our review that the console versions were capped at 30fps. Here's an excerpt from the email we received: "For the question about technical reasoning behind running at 30fps: For the Remaster, assets were brought to a higher resolution or even remade to be on par with modern standards. This, coupled also with a new rendering pipeline with GI and post-processes, makes it more taxing for Gen8 consoles. Please note that PS4 Pro and XBox One X run the build at 4k upscaling from 1440p. Aside from this, on PC, the framerate is not locked. And for the question on Xbox One X / PS4 Pro framerates: Pro Consoles will be running at native 1440p (2560x1440) at 30FPS. Temporal upsampling to 4k output from 1440p. (Side Note: The base consoles will be running at native 1080p output at 30FPS.) Also: The Pro Consoles will offer higher resolution and HDR on XBox One X, PS4 and PS4 Pro (side note: HDR will not be supported on XBox One and XBox One S)." We apologize for the error, but this does not change our 7/10 verdict.

Author: @LeonConner
Comment: This review doesn't do the game justice. I bought the game on a gut instinct as a digital download for $40 and I do not regret it. The combat isn't as bad as he implies. I have actual strategy that works in combat, that usually involves parrying attacks and out maneuvering the enemies moves. For a game not just developed, but also produced by an unknown new company, this game is awesome. I feel like this could be a new Fable, but better. That limited travel areas (like the first Fable game) definitely shows that they didn't want to put to much into yet. I think that if they get the support there is potential for an awesome RPG. The companions are more useful than this review shows, too. The first one is a healer, so if you tank appropriately then she won't die and she can keep you alive, and for the few times that my companion did die, I could easily just finish off what was left so she could come back. My favorite companion is Edwen though, she is awesomely powerful with spells, and can stun enemies for a few seconds, I've even seen her stun bosses. I have been playing on the Xbox 360, and I have noticed a few small glitches but nothing major, the camera can be a pain at times in the tighter area but with the free camera controls it's an easy fix. Granted $40 does seem to be a little much for it, but I still don't regret spending it. I would definitely recommend grabbing this game. The story is nice, the graphics are better than the first Fable (not hard I know, but non the less it's there) and the companions aren't as lively as say Bioware characters, but that's my own fault for being spoiled by Bioware's RPG awesomeness. The companions do have personalities of their own, react to what you do, and have their own little stories to tell, if your willing to ask. The voice acting is bad either. I would say this game get's more like a 7 out of 10. I see great potential with these companies, I hope I'm not the only one that sees that and is willing to help them hopefully finance another game.

Author: @therealCG62
Comment:
The grind really is abysmal. Going from fifth rates (what i was sailing in that big fight, which put me squarely in the "baby ships" category) to fourth rates is going to cost me 400xp. You get maybe 20xp per fight if you tackle somebody who actually stands a chance of sinking you, and more like 10xp if you just bully smaller boats. Even a relatively one-sided fight can extend on past ten minutes when you're talking fifth rate vs. sixth rate because you just don't have the broadside weight to sink the enemy quickly. So worst case scenario you're looking at a double digit number of hours spent grinding just to go from a small ship to a somewhat less small ship.

The grind is also brutal starting out. The ship you start with is effectively worthless, IMO- terrible piddly guns, tiny crew, paper-thin planking, and you don't even have the cargo space to do trading stuff. Once you graduate into a "proper" ship it's better, but man the new player experience is rough.

Author: @miskee11
Comment:
This video provides valuable perspective to all the people who take Half-Life engine mechanics for granted due to years of experience playing Counter-Strike/HL. To me this game is easy, because I've played climbing maps based on the exact same engine for well over a decade. The people who made this game are also veterans with several years of experience. This experience may have given the developers a little bit of tunnel vision...

Kreedz has been a popular game mod in CS 1.6 since ~2004, and every climber transitioning from CS to Kreedz Climbing will quickly adapt to the minor differences, but videos like this really show the value of focusing on the basics first. This mod is so full of techniques and skills to master that it will literally take months to get a grasp of what it has to offer, and if it's too hard from the start, new players will simply walk away. This is a bad thing for the game, because people need to get hooked from the start.

I watched your video, and based on your gameplay, the tutorial failed to teach you the basics of KZ movement, and that's why it was so frustratingly difficult for you to proceed. Jumping further actually takes a lot of skill, dexterity, technique and hand synchronization/speed. Even a single jump with one air strafe (i.e. one turn) may be difficult to master for a new player, because you need to learn 1. the prestrafe [i.e. the ground movement prior to jumping] 2. jump timing [jumps that have steep drops also have edge friction which requires you to jump earlier than usual; jump timing also affects your jump-off angle and the curve of your first strafe], 3. the strafe [which requires you to instantly let go of W as you jump, and then continue pressing either A or D and moving your mouse in synchronization with the key press] 4. duck timing [if you tuck your legs in too early, your strafes will not work; if you don't tuck, you probably won't make the jump]. The most important thing for beginners to learn is the prestrafe, as gaining proper running speed alone can help you go from 215 units to 235 units, and if you don't duck, you'll lose about 20 units of distance (the exact value depends on your horizontal velocity).

A regular jump & duck will only take you 215 units forward, but the best players in the world have used jumping techniques to jump 274-275 units on flat ground (and 273 block). A beginner can quickly learn how to make 235-240 unit jumps if they have a teacher. With some practice you can jump 245-250 with practically every jump, and with special techniques you may be able to do 255-260 fairly reliably. For perspective: it took me several months to do a 250 longjump and 255 countjump (another jumping technique) back in 2007 when I was a new player, and I had some help from fellow players, too. In 2011 I finally landed the 256 longjump block (shared Finnish record) after playing the game for several years.

This game also has various game mods that have slightly differing game mechanics, such as surfing. Surf maps use a higher air acceleration value, because the sliding ramps simply work better this way, but the acceleration value change also allows you to make quicker turns and strafe while ducked. In the standard climbing mod you can't make super fast and sharp turns without losing momentum, and you can't properly strafe while ducked. This makes learning even more difficult.

I'd recommend this game to anyone who has played deathrun, hide-n-seek, surf, slide, Kreedz or bunnyhop maps in CS/HL before, because this game combines it all into a single experience. New players would be great to have, but it just might end up being too intimidating to them.

Author: @binho2224
Comment:
Yeah, great concepts, graphics are fine (reminds me of those old days of web flash games). But the combat execution seems poor. A miss opportunity  to give characters different skills and attacks and mix up the combat. 

Remember that game I told you I was making with game maker? In it, You started with one character, enemies would occasionally drop what I called hero coins (HC), with enough hero coins you could buy a new character. Each one of them had 5 special skills that consumed mana and a unique fury state (which would build up by hitting enemies and could be unleashed for a limited time by pressing F).  After each level you would face a boss (they always dropped at least one hero coin) and go back to the hub where you could by the characters, also unlocking the next level. You could replay beaten lvls to grind, as characters would lvl up and increase their stats (I was also starting to program an equipment system). The penalty for dying was losing some of your precious hero coins, but the characters would retain their lvl. I guess it was becoming more of a type of action RPG than a Beat em up per say, as the combat was also simple, the variety coming from the unique set of skills.

Anyway, I'm saying all this because Knights of Braveland reminded me quite a bit of my own game for many reasons and I saw some things they could implement from what I was doing.

Comment: This seems like it could perhaps work in a "real world" or alternate history sort of campaign. If you have ever paid attention to real Europe, there are many tiny states--most of them style themselves as "grand duchies" or "principalities", even to the present day. I'm thinking (in the modern real world) Luxembourg, Lichtenstein, Andorra, San Marino, the Basque region on the border between Spain and France, the island of Malta, any remote hard-to-get-to places such as the Celtic areas of the continent like Brittany on the western coasts of France or Galicia in North western Spain. These places nearly all have a long history of repeated occupations by regional powers (the region known as Luxembourg went back and forth between France, Germany, and independence for centuries, and the language Luxembourgisch--a dialect of German heavily inflected by French--is spoken in Luxembourg and also by numerous small populations in the border regions of Belgium, France and Germany). That's all as a "for example". In Switzerland, Italian, French, and German are all spoken (as well as the uniquely Swiss language, Helvetian) because all three powers claimed (but really never conquered) Switzerland, going all the way back to Rome. This setting could be easily stuck into a campaign set between WW1 and WW2, or perhaps immediately prior to WW1, in the Swiss Alps. Perhaps as part of a Call of Cthulhu campaign, or an Indiana Jones type of pulp adventure campaign. You choose the MOST interesting indie rpg material to review, bar none.

Author: @bruhbruh-uv5fl
Comment:
Imo Blacksquad has been the best F2P shooter period. Growing up playing F2P games, it’s like a true nostalgia trip back to the OG F2P games like Soldier Front, AVA, Sudden Attack, Combat Arms, BlackShot, CS GO so on and so forth. It’s fast paced, it’s fun, adrenaline inducing and it makes you salty. 

I was hoping to find a game that had a mix of the old shooters and the current COD-like games and BlackSquad fits that. It’s like a breath of fresh air. 
But I just wish the devs, like what everyone says focus on optimisation, gun balancing and to me, map redesigns. It’ll just feel perfect like what Devs do for games like Warframe. 

One thing I’ll recognise first is that Blacksquad is meant to be Casual and not Competitive in any means, it was designed in terms of gameplay to give you choices by your skill level. I’ve been playing consistently for more than a year so lot of my complaints are something you see long term and not short. But continuing...

The maps are smaller in TDM and you’re given like 3 nades every spawn. I can get like around 5 -10 made kills a game just by spamming it. The spawn to site routes in demolition for some maps are so damn simple you already know when to expect them to come, where they are going to come from in like 1-3 matches *in a game*. You spend more time killing than strategising. The problem with that? Games like AVA focus on gun control (before P2W guns took over), games like soldier front focus on movement control/dexterity (crouch walking/silent sniper shots) Blacksquad gives alternatives to people with shit gun control by giving us the ‘pee guns.’ Movement is fast but normal. So after a while you notice it’s a mash of everything and tweaked to an extent. But what it’s left with is a lack of depth. There’s no core mechanic that jumps out to me, it’s balanced to say the most but there’s a lack of depth. If the maps are sophisticated, it adds a new element similar to CS GO. BS will become more tactical, thinking about taking the most advantageous position rather than taking the choke points where you know the enemy is going to come out. In Demo rarely do games exceed the 1 minute mark and feels more like a shortened TDM than what demo is supposed to feel like. It’s supposed to have that hook, that competitiveness that’ll get gamers addicted to the game for a long time. 

Alright for Gun balances, to me it doesn’t stick out as much when I’m playing casually but when you wanna be competitive  ‘Pee guns’ like R5, MDR, ACR are just plain ridiculous and are not punished enough. It’s more of a problem in TDM than demo as you’re almost guaranteed a win in a head on fight if you’re using like an AK12. But in a fast situations or game modes like TDM where an enemy might be right around a corner. Spraying pee blindly around said corner has no negatives. Spraying is supposed to be punished but shit like the GODAMN MDR DRILLS A BLOODY HOLE IN YOU CHEST ALL THE WAY BACK TO YOUR ANCESTORS. Okay so where I’m getting at is that BS doesn’t really have a steep learning curve unless you deliberately go for high recoil high damage guns.

The graphics are horrible. The performance for such poor graphics are even worse.   Physics is ..hilarious - not in a good way.
The dev didnt even know what exclusive fullscreen mode means.   The game cant decide or understand what windowed mode is, fullscreen, borderless, etc etc.

Sure some people (mostly shills, and those already wasted money on it) will keep defending it. Ofcourse they will.     But the negative reviews should really be taken seriously, this game is NOT close to be worthy of that price tag.   This pile of dung, is worth maybe $5-8  at best.
But as I said, I feel mostly sorry for the devs working on this game.  I dont think they really wanted this to be in EA yet.      Do know that the publisher has barely any good game under the belt. Their 'best' being Medieval Dynasty.     But that's it, the rest of their library is just a horrible arcade-ish kinda games.   Yes they are not proper arcade game, but what I mean is, the control and gameplay FEELS arcadish.   Very stiff and clunky gameplay and movements.  This game is just like those other games (exception being MD).

Does this game deserve that massive negative opinion it has at the moment? Yes, oh hundred times yes.   
People gotta stop defending trash like this with "but it's EA it needs time to mature".   FFS,  make the game at least somewhat playable and enjoyable BEFORE releasing it on EA.   Right now, what the devs/publisher has done, is made some people pay waaaay too much money, to beta...no alpha test the game for them.
I would buy this again if it was $5.   But the current pricetag, for this trash? The balls of this publisher. Yikes.
Meanwhile you have the devs, working their butts off(hopefully) to make this a good and cool game.   And now they see how much dislike their game is getting. It gotta be a kick to the morale for them.  All because this horrible publisher got greedy, and threw this game out on EA  mooooonths before it was ready for the public.
I would say to anyone considering buying this...just go throw the money in the nearest toilet.  It's literally the same sh-t.
Return maybe late 2024, then this game might be somewhat enjoyable.
The devs will most likely release tons of patches in the coming days and weeks.  And people will lose their smarts again and go "see, they listen, they're fixing the game, told all you haters it would be good".     Seriously, everything in life, be it a product, or a person, only gets ONE first impression.   This impression this game has given the 'world' right now, will stick with them for a long long time.  And it will affect the sales.    Which is sad, because IF (no guarantee) this game ends up becoming really good in a year or two,  people would still avoid it due to the massive dislike ratio to it.
So as I said, they have shot themselves in the foot here.   
Everything in the game atm, is either broken, so super dumb.     On occasions the game tries to be funny. Like there's a couple of NPC's either singing a line from a song, or referencing to something in the Real world.   Problem is, this is the Wild West,  but they're refering to things that happened maybe in the year 2018 or something.    Like that npc that sings a line of a certain song, that I believe came out around 2017 or thereabouts. How the f-ck would this NPC know of this song a century before it was made?    It's ok they try to be funny, but this is really bad. And for those trying to immerse themselves, it's really hard.   Say this is at the end of 1800 something,  lets say 1890 (honestly dunno what year this is supposed to be),   how can someone in 1890 know of a song that comes out in 2017?   Immersion is out the window.  Though, its impossible to immerse yourself in this game to begin with lol.    
Cut down trees, and watch they fly away like a rocket.      I had floating trees and stones here and there.    There's SO many bugs.   Which makes me certain that this is not even out of pre-alpha.  Yet greed made them put this on steam, to make money from 'not-so-smart' gamers.
But thankfully people were ready to give honest bad reviews for the game.  That will hopefully teach this horrible publisher a thing or two.  Probably not though.

This game might be worth checking in on again somewhere at the end of 2024 at the earliest.   As I do hope this will turn into a gem eventually.  There's not enough games of this type in this setting.
As mentioned, its sad that this wasnt made by the same team that made MD.  Because right now, the current devs, really do come off as two high school kids releasing a project they slapped together over the weekend.

Author: @varsoonhks3211
Comment:
"I don't know who this is catering to."
It's me. It's catering to me.

SaGa Frontier is my favorite RPG of all time. I love that it respects the player's time and intelligence and that campaigns are only 6 to 10 hours long.

I loved SaGa Scarlet Grace. It was easily the RPG of decade for me, completely revitalizing my interest in turn based complexity while also proving how much useless chaff could be cut from an RPG. Gone were pointless treks through forgettable dungeons, filler encounters, and hours of downtime. Everything felt purposeful and I had agency to take myriad paths in forging my own adventure.

Emerald Beyond is the Frontier to Scarlet Grace's Romancing SaGa. It is a fusion of all of my favorite parts of both the aforementioned games.
When you say you're focused on the narrative because that's "all this game is", you're missing the forest for the trees. Emerald Beyond is as much its branching-path choose-your-own-adventure, make-of-it-what-you-will evocative adventure as it is an excellent exploration of one of the most enjoyable combat systems in any RPG.

I wouldn't blame anyone for failing to grok the systems in place, but almost all your critiques of the battle system fall flat. It sounds like you got hosed by interrupts because you didn't build a team that could quell them. The whole "You should just throw the turn" mentality is so incongruous with the actual systems at play, especially when many of those big several interrupt turns make for perfect turns to begin channeling spells, too. So, naturally, it made sense that you wouldn't like how spells need to channel for their powerful effects and combo potential, especially if you're failing to incorporate them in battle such to the extent that you're prepping a spell when you know you can end the encounter before the channel time finishes. The whole 'you get lucky' angle is an exciting aspect of the system, but relying on it to defeat difficult battles is also a recipe for disaster--you could just instead learn what the enemy weaknesses are, what they always take critical damage from, and set your team up properly before a fight to exploit those weaknesses. Maybe I've got much more of a understanding of these systems because I put a lot of time into Scarlet Grace, which this system builds off of, but approaching this game like it's any other JRPG or even any other SaGa game is a recipe for a bad time. Learn its systems, read the tips and glossaries afforded you, actually consider your team members and even what benched party members can do to offer variety in strategies, consider your formations and how dynamically they can affect what you're capable of in a fight. I think it's wild that you would bring up the combat system but not mention some of its most standout features, such as Overdrives, Showstoppers, and how even bosses follow the same weakness and resistance rules that basic enemy types do. There's a similar sense that you really didn't comprehend how the mechanics worked when talking about the trading system, as no guides are needed to parse that you post an item and you are offered other items of relative equal or lesser value. Completing another battle just refreshes the items offered for a different set. I don't particularly feel like this is some huge personal failing on your behalf--the game could absolutely use better modes of conveying all of the mechanics I'd mentioned here, but it feels bad to see someone so critically lambast an RPG I've loved for a myriad of issues that aren't problems I experienced at all. If anything, my biggest critique of battles is that there's less information for what is available to be learned and worked towards than in Scarlet Grace and that the Item Trading and Sensei Trials both require a little too much micro management between each and every fight for how incrementally those systems reward you.

Speaking of the actual plot--I liked piecing together the larger significance of what was happening in these worlds and across them through the multiple playthroughs of different protagonists. This game does something I've seen in hardly any RPG before, where a second playthrough differs massively from the first--not just in terms of options available for worlds to go to, but also in the stories told in those worlds and even the stories told within the main adventure unique to that protagonist. Sadly, I think that a lot of people, even fans of SaGa, are going to miss out on this massive aspect of the game solely because there's so much of an attitude of 'Why do a second playthrough on a character?' especially when you have different protagonists to choose and play through as well. In my experience, though, when I finished Tsunanori's story for the first time, I did not feel the catharsis I am used to from a SaGa game--I wanted to spend more time with him and my team of Kugutsu. So I did a second adventure and it felt much more a *continuation* of his story rather than a repeat. I was amazed.

Emerald Beyond is a 10/10 game for me and I can see myself easily dumping 300+ hours into it and coming back over the years as I usually do with Frontier, especially given the short nature of the character campaigns here as well. Got an evening to kill? Time to give a certain character another playthrough, maybe try out a different team setup, see what options I'm given, try to take some new routes. That's awesome. This review, though, seems like such a surface-level skim that was pushed out after engaging primarily with the first playthrough of a single protagonist's plot. The failure to discuss those larger cross-character links, NG+ discoveries, and how the worlds are developed through the different protagonist perspectives all speaks towards a low level of engagement with the game as a whole. Given there's no Siugnas footage here and the majority of what is presented is from the single first playthrough of the duo cop plotline with only opening segments of others shown, it's hard to take this review as reflective of an opinion of someone who has actually played the whole game. Instead, it really comes off as though you've played about a tenth of what's on offer and bounced off of it really hard. 

For you, though, I'd suggest trying out Scarlet Grace if you haven't. Outside of Leonard's story, I'm sure that the more linear and straightforward narratives as well as focus on deuteragonists might do well to give a little of what you felt was missing in this one. Side characters, yes, will continue to be mostly expressed in battle dialogue and expressive voicelines, but there's far more emergent character plots from regional narratives. It seems the more grounded high fantasy adventure will also provide a little more context that might satisfy that want for a more actualized world rather than the fragmented Regions that Emerald Beyond has on offer.

I understand your opinion but I disagree strongly with this review. The battle system in this game is stellar: imo it is one of the best in jrpgs and builds upon what made scarlet saga great, while eschewing the aspects or scarlet saga that sucked. The story is disjointed but not as bad as this review makes it sound. Some of the world's stories and lore are very interesting imo and a big part of the pleasure for me in playing through these is that you have different options and the game is nonlinear. I like this element of choice and I think replay value or just trying different things is huge here. I loved the area where you choose who lives or dies with unfreezing them. Contrary to this review, the game does tell you some details on the people you are unfreezing, so it becomes a trolley problem moral dilemma. The world with the alien flower people by far was my favorite and while the story did not have deep significance for bonnie and formina, I feel like the story in of itself was good and I enjoyed the experience.

In terms of who this appeals to, in my opinion anybody who is tired of generic jrpgs and wants a different experience. Anybody who wants a good battle system that requires some thought and strategy and a nonlinear choose your own adventure kind of game. This game imo is way better than a 5.5/10. Although the graphics could have been better, the game itself is really fun. Battles are enjoyable and challenging and while the worlds arent very interconnected, individually several of them have interesting stories to tell.

Author: @Devonaxx
Comment:
Few things to know about the game:

1) developers are Chinese and are an indie company of around 9 people.
2) There is NO offline play.. this is ALWAYS ONLINE.. Yes, this means that without internet you can't play the game.
3) When you accept their terms (EULA) by playing the game, you give them permission to read out your PC (internet speeds, provider, computer hardware, etc.)
4) There is no "sandbox mode" that makes it so all research is already unlocked. There is also no PVP mode where you can play against friends or other players.
5) The amount you can zoom out (and see  more of the map) is very short. Don't expect to be able to see your whole main base.
6) Mack says in this video @3:23 that there are many different game-modes, there are 2.. Survival (wave based) and Last Stand (rogue-lite elements).
7) The training/tutorial in this game is VERY short and is missing A LOT of stuff.
8) Not counting the tutorial map, there are 4 maps on Survival. There is no map choice in Last stand.
9) There are 2 hero's to pick in Survival and 2 OTHER hero's in Last Stand.
10) There is an "armory" system that you unlock after playing 1 real match. This allows you to earn points each match that you can use to purchase buffs and upgrades in the main menu. Like getting more money after each wave or start with more money or power or oil. these can then be activated (max of 3) when you choose your hero.
11) Even though we have access to the workshop, there are NO mods for this game yet. I can't wait for the mods that allow further zoom, Increase build range and allow gun towers to be placed closer together.
12) In Survival you can kill every alien on the map. Do this before the final wave comes because when the final wave comes EVERY alien on the map (2500+) comes towards your base + the spawned wave as well. So prepare yourself.
13) There is no ROTATING buildings or the map. You will always look from one angle. The only thing you can rotate is the gate you can build for your walls. (only 1 hero in survival can build walls).
14) You are not allowed to repair damaged structures (and thus walls or turrets) when you are under attack. I do not know if this is only in survival.
15) the game's size is 8.79 GB when fully downloaded and installed.

If you have any specific questions about the game so you know if you want to buy or not, let me know.
I will add reply to this message if I remember other bits of information to share.

Once on the newer one; however, you are still yourself, with the same quests so you can indeed complete them. In addition, prior to venturing far from a town prior to being able to take on those skeletons and wraiths, you can flee towards a town and let the guards help you take them out for some powerful loot. I always found these creatures a treasure trove and not a creature to complain about. I liked the game better than Conan or Ark. My only real beef with the game is that creatures can spawn in your base when you are off line. Multiple times I found a wide range of hostile mobs in my keep with no gaps in the walls, sometimes even town guards found a way inside.  The game is far from perfect, yet I keep going back to it. Usually I play on an off-line manner any more, as I am quite fickle as to what I want to play and when, and always found the decay rate on buildings high enough that often my work was all (or mostly all) gone when I decided to pop back in. Single player freezes time when you are not playing so that is not an issue. However, with time frozen like that growing crops is a bit of an issue... Cheers, and thanks again for reviewing this abandoned game.

I honestly feel conflicted about this game.

I mean it doesn't look bad on itself, it really looks a hell of fun. The only issue I have is that this game belong to the Anomaly series.

I mean, Anomaly debuted as the opossite of the Tower Defense Genere, a Tower OFFENSE Game, it basically took the clasic TD formula and spin it around 360°.

Anomaly Warzone Earth establish the bases of this game and sub genere and Anomaly 2 expand it adding cool new mechanics and gimicks like 5 units that can "Morph" (Basically pull out a Transformers) between vehicle and walker/mech mode wich change the way these units function completely basically giving you 10 units in total, ranging from simple stuff like, a fragile yet powerfull long rage with slow fire rate hover tank that can only fire in a 30° cone that transforns into quadrupedal walker with a rocket launcher that can fire in a 360° radious with a higher rate of fire but has less range and damage, or a mini tanks that has two medium range miniguns that can quickly shred enemies and does more damage the longer it stays in combat wich transforms into a bipedal mech that has two flame trowers that can fire independently and continiously to two enemies at the same time and has more health but has limited range. Or a small hover aircraft that can shield the two units in front and back of it and transforms into a spider mech that slows down the towers fire rate and rotation speed and has lot of healt

God the Morphing mechanic is one of my favorite mechanics ever.

The point is ... Anomaly as a franchise build it's name by taking the classic tower defense formula and twisting it around completely and creating and brand new original sub genere ... And then 11 Bit studious decide to end the franchise by turning it into the opossite of what it was ... By removing what made the franchise special and turning it into another tower defense game ...

Look. Point one, I am not sayinf the shouldn't have done Anomaly Defenders, Point two, I am not saying that 11 bit is a bad game studio and, Point Three I am not saying that Anomaly Denfender is a Bad Game, I am just saying that (And this only my personal opinion) they should have keep the unique and original formula of the first two games and then add something like an alternative campaing or an arcade mode where you can play as the machines and that way you have both worlds together, a Tower Defense Game and the classic Anomaly Tower Offense.

Again I am not saying that Anomaly Defenders is a bad game, in fact I actually recomended.

But I just wish we could see more of this franchise and more of this unique and fun sub genere it created.

Tower Offense ... Huh. I wonder why no one has ever tought of that before or made more like that.

Gues Anomaly just like to break molds
